Wayland · Parity · regolith-wm-config 4.13.1 · regolith-wm-config#82

Looks without a wallpaper picture define colours (regolith.wallpaper.color.primary, …secondary, …shading.type). sway showed black for colour names and drew no gradients.

  1. With the default look and no wallpaper picture set, look at the desktop.

You should see: a vertical grey gradient, as in the X11 session.

Looks in their own style everywhere

X11 and Wayland · regolith-wm-config 4.13.1, regolith-ftue 2.2.4 · regolith-wm-config#88, regolith-ftue#10

  1. Open the Look Selector with super alt l.

You should see: the selector in the colours of your look, like the launcher. The keybinding help shown on your first login uses the look’s style too.

Updated Dracula, Nord and Nevil themes

X11 and Wayland · dracula-gtk 4.0.0, nordic 2.2.0, whitesur-gtk-theme 1.2 · dracula-gtk#3, nordic#3, WhiteSur-gtk-theme#4

The GTK themes of the Dracula, Nord and Nevil looks are new upstream releases.

  1. Run sudo apt install regolith-look-dracula.
  2. Pick dracula in the Look Selector (super alt l), and run gsettings get org.gnome.desktop.interface gtk-theme.

You should see: 'Dracula', with the Dracula icons. Pick your usual look again afterwards.

Workspace names with accents and other non-ASCII text

X11 and Wayland · regolith-session 1.3.1 · regolith-session#85

  1. Add wm.workspace.02.name: 2:Ñandú café to ~/.config/regolith3/Xresources.
  2. Log out and in again, and press super 2.

You should see: “Ñandú café” on the workspace button, not escape codes.

Removing an override takes effect without logging out

X11 and Wayland · regolith-session 1.3.1 · regolith-session#98

  1. Add wm.bar.position: top to ~/.config/regolith3/Xresources and press super shift r.
  2. Remove the line and press super shift r again.

You should see: the bar move to the top, then back to the bottom. In 3.4 a removed value stayed until the next login.

Settings app

The shortcut list matches the session

X11 and Wayland · regolith-control-center 1.50.5 · regolith-control-center#30

Open Settings (super c) › Keyboard › View and Customize Shortcuts.

You should see:

  • X11: a Screenshots section with the keys the session really uses (print saves a screenshot, and so on), so you can change them.
  • Wayland: no Navigation, Windows or Screenshots sections, because sway handles those keys.

Sessions and first login

No GNOME welcome wizard

X11 and Wayland · regolith-session 1.3.1 · regolith-session#70

Create a user and log in to a Regolith session for the first time.

You should see: the Regolith keybinding help, and no GNOME “Welcome” window.

The X11 compositor works without 3D acceleration

X11 · regolith-compositor-picom-glx 1.4.1 · regolith-compositor-picom-glx#17, regolith-compositor-picom-glx#16, fixes regolith-compositor-picom-glx#4

In virtual machines and on machines that render in software, picom now uses its xrender backend, and it starts again if it crashes.

  1. Run pgrep -a picom.
  2. Run kill -9 $(pgrep -x picom), wait a few seconds, and run pgrep -a picom again.

You should see: picom running (with --backend xrender on a software renderer), and running again with a new process ID.

item.title: Verify behavior against upstream
item.description:
Regolith is composed of several existing open-source projects plus some additional custom packages. Sometimes when a bug is found in Regolith, actually it’s a bug in an upstream project. Determining the source of bugs is a first step in getting them fixed.

Check gnome-flashback

Most of the GNOME support in Regolith’s X11 session (regolith-session-flashback) comes from the gnome-flashback project. To run a gnome-flashback session, install the session and log back in to your account after selecting that session from the login screen.

  1. Install the gnome-session-flashback session:

    sudo apt install gnome-session-flashback

    apt also removes regolith-session-flashback-ext, which conflicts with gnome-session-flashback. On Ubuntu 26.04 the Regolith X11 session keeps working without it.

  2. Log out. On the login screen, select your user, choose the GNOME Flashback (Metacity) session (in GDM, from the gear button in the lower-right corner), and log in.

  3. Verify your behavior against Regolith. If the problematic behavior also exists in gnome-flashback then the bug is likely there. If the bug does not exist in the gnome-flashback then it’s likely to be in Regolith.

  4. When you are done, log back into the Regolith / X11 session. To remove the GNOME Flashback session again, reinstall the package it replaced:

    sudo apt install regolith-session-flashback-ext

Wayland session

The Wayland session (regolith-session-sway) does not use gnome-flashback. It runs Regolith’s build of Sway (sway-regolith, which replaces Ubuntu’s sway package) together with GNOME services such as gnome-settings-daemon. To check whether a problem comes from a GNOME application or service, compare with the GNOME session of your distribution, if it is installed. Problems with window management are more likely to be in Sway or in Regolith’s configuration.
